# Dialog

Header: `winui/ui/dialogs/Dialog.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/dialogs/Dialog.hpp`.

A modal dialog over the whole window, with a title, arbitrary content and up to three buttons.

It isn't placed in the tree. Hand it to [Window::show_modal()](../tree/window.md#show_modal), which takes ownership and routes all input to it until it closes. [Tab](tabs.md#uitab) moves only between the dialog's controls, and focus goes back where it was afterward. The buttons are always Primary, Secondary, Close from left to right, whatever order they were set in.

The [default_button()](#default_button) is accented and clicked by an Enter that nothing else in the dialog uses. Escape clicks the Close button, or closes with Close when there is none. Every button and Escape close the dialog. [on_closing()](#on_closing) runs first and may cancel. Then the window takes the dialog down, and [on_closed()](#on_closed) reports the result once it is gone. [Window::close_modal()](../tree/window.md#close_modal) closes it from outside, reporting None. With no default button set, the primary button is the default when there is one. A dialog whose primary button destroys something sets Close or None instead.

The dialog is at least 320x184 and at most 548x756 DIPs, unless its [`width`](../tree/element.md#width), [`max_width`](../tree/element.md#max_width), [`height`](../tree/element.md#height) or [`max_height`](../tree/element.md#max_height) say otherwise. It fades in over 250 ms.

Example: 
```cpp
auto dialog = std::make_unique<ui::DialogControl>();
dialog->set_title("Close without saving?");
dialog->set_content(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Your changes will be lost."));
dialog->set_primary_button("Close", nullptr);
dialog->set_close_button("Cancel", nullptr);
dialog->set_default_button(ui::DialogDefaultButton::Close);
dialog->on_closed([&](ui::DialogResult result) {
    if (result == ui::DialogResult::Primary)
        quit();
});
window.show_modal(std::move(dialog));

// Declaratively:
bool busy = false;
window.show_modal(ui::Dialog{
    .title          = "Close without saving?",
    .default_button = ui::DialogDefaultButton::Close,
    .primary        = {.text = "Close"},
    .close          = {.text = "Cancel"},
    .on_closing     = [&](const ui::DialogClosingArgs& args)
    { return args.result == ui::DialogResult::Primary && busy ? ui::Cancel : ui::Proceed; },
    .on_closed = [&](ui::DialogResult result)
    {
        if (result == ui::DialogResult::Primary)
            quit();
    },
    .content = ui::Text{.text = "Your changes will be lost."},
});
```

## `ui::Dialog`

A modal dialog. Builds a [ui::DialogControl](#uidialogcontrol), which a caller then hands to [Window::show_modal()](../tree/window.md#show_modal).

Every button and Escape close the dialog by themselves. on_closing runs first and may cancel, for example while a save is still running. Then on_closed reports the result once the dialog is gone.

Example: 
```cpp
window.show_modal(ui::Dialog{
    .title          = "Close without saving?",
    .default_button = ui::DialogDefaultButton::Close,
    .primary        = {.text = "Close"},
    .close          = {.text = "Cancel"},
    .on_closed      = [&](ui::DialogResult result) {
        if (result == ui::DialogResult::Primary)
            quit();
    },
    .content        = ui::Text{.text = "Your changes will be lost."},
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::Dialog{
    .title, .default_button, .primary, .secondary, .close, .style, .margin, .width, .height,
    .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment,
    .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .accessibility, .on_closing, .on_closed,
    .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down,
    .on_wheel, .control, .content
}
```

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| <span id="uidialog-default_button"></span>`default_button` | `ui::Binding<std::optional<ui::DialogDefaultButton>>` |  | The default button: accented, and clicked by an Enter nothing else in the dialog uses. Unset makes it the primary button when there is one, and no button otherwise. |

| <span id="uidialog-secondary"></span>`secondary` | `ui::DialogButton` |  | The middle button; closes with DialogResult::Secondary. |
| <span id="uidialog-close"></span>`close` | `ui::DialogButton` |  | The right-hand button, also clicked by Escape; closes with DialogResult::Close. |
| <span id="uidialog-on_closing"></span>`on_closing` | `ui::Callback<ui::Decision(const ui::DialogClosingArgs&)>` |  | Gets the result of every close before it happens; return [ui::Cancel](../core/namespace-ui.md#cancel) to keep the dialog open. |

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<Element> build()&&
```

Consumes the spec and returns the built [ui::DialogControl](#uidialogcontrol); the caller owns it.

## `ui::DialogButton`

One of a dialog's up-to-three buttons. Left default (empty text) means "no such button".

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<bool> can_save{false};
ui::DialogButton   save_button{ .text = "Save", .enabled = can_save, .on_click = [&] { save(); } };
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::DialogButton{
    .text, .enabled, .on_click
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uidialogbutton-text"></span>`text` | `std::string` |  | The button's caption; empty leaves the button out. |
| <span id="uidialogbutton-on_click"></span>`on_click` | `ui::Action` |  | Fired on click, before the dialog starts closing. |

Plus the common fields `enabled` every spec carries ([conventions](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec)).

### operator bool

```cpp
operator bool() const
```

True when the button exists, which means it has a caption.

## `ui::DialogControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`.

A modal dialog over the whole window, with a title, arbitrary content and up to three buttons.

It isn't placed in the tree. Hand it to [Window::show_modal()](../tree/window.md#show_modal), which takes ownership and routes all input to it until it closes. ### DialogControl

```cpp
DialogControl()
```

An empty dialog: no title, no content, no buttons.

### set_title

```cpp
void set_title(std::string title)
```

Sets the heading above the content (UTF-8), drawn 20 DIPs, semibold and wrapping.

### title

```cpp
const std::string& title() const
```

The title; empty by default. Screen readers also use it as the name when none is set.

### set_content

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* set_content(std::unique_ptr<T> content)
```

Takes ownership of the body content and returns a non-owning observer to it, the same convention as [StackControl::add()](../layout/stack.md#add). Each further call appends below the previous content.

### set_primary_button

```cpp
ButtonControl* set_primary_button(std::string text, Callback<void()> on_click)
```

Sets the primary (leftmost) button, which closes with Primary. Each button's click runs `on_click` (if any), then closes the dialog with its result. Calling one again replaces that button. The visual order is fixed whatever order these are called in. Returns the button as a non-owning observer, owned by the dialog. `on_click` may be null.

### set_secondary_button

```cpp
ButtonControl* set_secondary_button(std::string text, Callback<void()> on_click)
```

Sets the secondary button, which closes with Secondary.

### set_close_button

```cpp
ButtonControl* set_close_button(std::string text, Callback<void()> on_click)
```

Sets the close button, also clicked by Escape, which closes with Close.

### primary_button

```cpp
ButtonControl* primary_button() const
```

The primary button, or nullptr when none was set.

### secondary_button

```cpp
ButtonControl* secondary_button() const
```

The secondary button, or nullptr when none was set.

### close_button

```cpp
ButtonControl* close_button() const
```

The close button, or nullptr when none was set.

### set_default_button

```cpp
void set_default_button(std::optional<DialogDefaultButton> button)
```

Sets the default button. It is drawn accented and clicked by an Enter that the focused element does not use itself (a [Button](button.md#uibutton), a list or a [TextBox](text-box.md#uitextbox) with a submit handler keep theirs). While focus is on one of the dialog's own buttons the accent follows focus instead. `std::nullopt` (the default) makes the primary button the default when there is one, and no button otherwise.

### default_button

```cpp
DialogDefaultButton default_button() const
```

The default button in effect: the one set, else Primary when there is a primary button, else None.

### hide

```cpp
void hide()
```

Close with `None` (on_closing still runs, and may cancel).

### result

```cpp
DialogResult result() const
```

What the last close reported; `None` until one happened.

### on_closing

```cpp
void on_closing(Callback<Decision(const DialogClosingArgs&)> handler)
```

Raised before every close with its result; return [ui::Cancel](../core/namespace-ui.md#cancel) to keep the dialog open (a Primary click on a form that does not validate, say).

### on_closed

```cpp
void on_closed(Callback<void(DialogResult)> handler)
```

Raised once the dialog is closed and out of the window, with what closed it. The dialog is destroyed by then, so the handler may show the next one. A dialog replaced by another show_modal() does not raise it.

### for_each_child

```cpp
void for_each_child(ChildVisitor visit) const override
```

Visits the title, the content host and the shown buttons, in visual order.

### collect_focusables

```cpp
void collect_focusables(std::vector<Element*>& out) override
```

Adds the content's focusable controls, then the shown buttons, to the dialog's tab order. The title is never a stop.

### default_focus

```cpp
Element* default_focus() override
```

Where focus starts: the first focusable thing in the content, else the default button.

### transition_opacity

```cpp
float transition_opacity() const override
```

The opening fade's opacity, rising linearly from 0 to 1 over 250 ms. The dimmed backdrop behind the dialog fades in with it. There is no closing fade. [Window::close_modal()](../tree/window.md#close_modal) removes the dialog and restores focus at once.

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

Always AutomationRole::Pane.

### automation_name_fallback

```cpp
std::string automation_name_fallback() const override
```

[title()](#title), used when [Accessibility::name](../tree/accessibility.md#name) is not set.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

The frame, title, content and button area, clamped between 320x184 and 548x756 DIPs. A width or max width set on the dialog replaces the 548, and a height or max height the 756. When the dialog is wider than 548, the buttons keep their size at 548 and group at the right.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Places the title and content, with 24 DIPs of padding and 12 DIPs apart, and the buttons in the button area. Three buttons take a third each, two a half each, and one alone the right half.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

Draws the frame, the title and content background, the button area and the children.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

Advances the open fade.

### key_override

```cpp
bool key_override(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

Enter the focused element had no use for: the default button's click, if it is enabled.

## struct DialogClosingArgs

What a [Dialog](#uidialog)'s `on_closing` gets: the result the close reports. The handler returns [ui::Cancel](../core/namespace-ui.md#cancel) to keep the dialog open.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `result` | `DialogResult` | `DialogResult::None` | Which button (or Escape) is closing it. |

## class DialogAwaiter

What `co_await ui::show_dialog(window, spec)` waits on; see [show_dialog()](#show_dialog).

### DialogAwaiter

```cpp
DialogAwaiter(Window& window, Dialog spec)
```

Holds `spec` until the coroutine suspends.

### await_ready

```cpp
bool await_ready() const noexcept
```

Never ready: the dialog is shown when the coroutine suspends.

### await_suspend

```cpp
void await_suspend(std::coroutine_handle<> coroutine)
```

Shows the dialog and hands `coroutine` to its close.

### await_resume

```cpp

```

## Enumerations

### DialogDefaultButton

```cpp
enum class DialogDefaultButton
```

Which button of a dialog is the default one.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `None` | No default button: Enter clicks nothing, no button is accented. |
| `Primary` | The primary (leftmost) button. |
| `Secondary` | The secondary button. |
| `Close` | The close (cancel) button. |

### DialogResult

```cpp
enum class DialogResult
```

What closed the dialog. The Close button and Escape report Close; hide() and [Window::close_modal()](../tree/window.md#close_modal) report None.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `None` | Closed from outside: hide() or [Window::close_modal()](../tree/window.md#close_modal). |
| `Primary` | Closed by the primary button. |
| `Secondary` | Closed by the secondary button. |
| `Close` | Closed by the Close button or Escape. |

## Functions

### show_dialog

```cpp
DialogAwaiter show_dialog(Window& window, Dialog spec)
```

Shows `spec` modally over `window` and lets a coroutine wait for the answer. `co_await ui::show_dialog(window, spec)` gives the [DialogResult](#dialogresult) the dialog closed with, so a flow of questions reads top to bottom without nested on_closed handlers. The spec's own on_closing, which may still cancel, and on_closed still run. on_closed runs before the coroutine goes on.

The coroutine resumes on the UI thread inside the window's next tick(), as after [on_ui_thread()](../tree/namespace-ui.md#on_ui_thread). When the dialog goes without an answer, the coroutine is dropped instead and its frame destroyed without resuming. That happens when another modal replaces the dialog, when the [Window](../tree/window.md) is destroyed with it open, or when the window is closed by the time the answer would resume it. A coroutine that has to clean up does it in a destructor, as with [on_ui_thread()](../tree/namespace-ui.md#on_ui_thread). Call it on the UI thread, from a coroutine such as a [ui::FireAndForget](../tree/fire-and-forget.md).

With MSVC, compute texts that come from a function call into local variables before the `co_await`. MSVC can destroy a temporary of a `co_await` expression too early, and the call that reads it crashes.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::FireAndForget delete_files(ui::Window& window, ui::Property<std::string>& status)
{
    const ui::DialogResult answer = co_await ui::show_dialog(window, ui::Dialog{
        .title          = "Delete 3 files?",
        .default_button = ui::DialogDefaultButton::Close,
        .primary        = {.text = "Delete"},
        .close          = {.text = "Cancel"},
        .content        = ui::Text{.text = "They go to the recycle bin."},
    });
    if (answer != ui::DialogResult::Primary)
        co_return;
    status = "Deleted";
}
```
